sections.markdown:
## A — Application documents, testing and license conditions
Issuer: Nebraska Department of Motor Vehicles is identified in this private handbook snapshot [A05].
The written-test description directs passenger-car permit and operator applicants to this manual [A19].
The section topic is application documents, testing and license conditions; First-time passenger-car application evidence, test requirements and license conditions are covered. Online service eligibility, military extensions, live contacts and changing fees are retained as administrative verification debt rather than stable rules.
Question count, passing standard, test duration, bank size and official weights remain unknown (verify NE-sec02-PASS).
Edition and effective-date status remain unresolved under the registrar observation-location rule; the recorded source liveness is verification debt. No official exam mirror is asserted.
Practice scoring is governed by the accepted learning-loop product policy; it does not supply an official passing standard.

sections.heading: Application documents, testing and license conditions
sections.markdown:
## B — Application documents, testing and license conditions
Audience: first-time Nebraska passenger-car applicants studying application documents, testing and license conditions.
First-time passenger-car application evidence, test requirements and license conditions are covered. Online service eligibility, military extensions, live contacts and changing fees are retained as administrative verification debt rather than stable rules.
Level: handbook-based preparation. Follow the learner, provisional or operator path that applies to the applicant; scope does not include motorcycle or commercial licensing. No extra prerequisites or official exam weights are inferred.

## C — Application documents, testing and license conditions

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A17
A Nebraska application requires at least 2 documents establishing the principal address. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A17
An applicant must disclose a verifiable Social Security number or establish the exemption with an unexpired I-94 or I-94A arrival-and-departure record in a valid foreign passport. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A17
New Nebraska applicants must establish U.S. citizenship or, for applicants who are not U.S. citizens, lawful status. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A17
After citizenship proof has been presented, it is not required again at later licensing-office visits. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A17
An applicant who is not a U.S. citizen must present lawful-status proof on every licensing-office visit. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A17
Required documents must be certified and bear a raised seal or stamp. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A17
A faxed document or photocopy is not accepted for the application. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A17
Document review may require more information and a later office visit rather than same-day approval. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A17
A document marked as unsuitable for identification proof cannot establish identity. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A17
The DMV may keep copies of documents submitted with an application. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A17
To link a changed name to the existing permit, license or ID, present certified marriage licenses, certified divorce decrees or a court order; lawful-status applicants may use a name-change petition. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A17
A state-government-certified birth certificate is an accepted citizenship-and-identity document. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A17
A birth certificate from a hospital is not accepted. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A17
A Puerto Rico birth certificate issued before September 30, 2010 is not accepted. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A17
An unexpired U.S. passport or passport card can establish citizenship and identity. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A17
An unexpired I-94 or I-94A is accepted for lawful status and identity with a valid foreign passport, except the passport is unnecessary for a Refugee stamp or Canadian place of origin; F1, F2, J1, J2, M1 and M2 applicants also need an I-20 and/or DS-2019, and a Refugee stamp may require an I-797. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A17
Applicants with F1, F2, J1, J2, M1 or M2 status must also supply an I-20 and/or DS-2019 for SEVIS information. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A17
For an I-94 or I-94A arrival record, the foreign passport is unnecessary when the record is stamped Refugee or the place of origin is Canada. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A17
A visa alone is not one of the accepted lawful-status and identity documents listed here. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A18
An unexpired permanent-resident card is an accepted lawful-status and identity document. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A18
An unexpired employment-authorization card is an accepted lawful-status and identity document. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A18
A Certificate of Naturalization on Form N-550 or N-570 is an accepted citizenship and identity document. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A18
The handbook lists a Certificate of Citizenship on Form N-560 or N-451 as citizenship and identity evidence. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A18
A State Department Consular Report of Birth Abroad on Form FS-240, DS-1350 or FS-545 is accepted as citizenship and identity evidence. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A18
Principal-address evidence must show the Nebraska address and come from 2 different issuing sources. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A18
A post-office box does not establish the principal residence address. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A18
An applicant younger than 21 who cannot supply personal residence proof may use the parent’s or guardian’s address documents. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A18
A bank or other financial-institution statement used for residence proof must have been issued within 90 days. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A18
A pay stub used for residence proof must be from the preceding 90 days and show the employer’s name and address. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A18
A government document used under the handbook’s recent-document category must have been issued within 90 days. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A18
A magazine used for residence proof must be from the preceding 90 days. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A18
A mailed envelope, box or postcard used as address proof must show a postmark or stamped date within 90 days. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A18
Correspondence, a receipt or an invoice used in the recent-address-document category must be dated within 90 days. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A18
A valid Nebraska vehicle registration is one accepted residence document. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A18
A valid insurance policy or card for life, health, auto or home coverage is one accepted residence document. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A18
A valid real-estate tax statement or receipt is one accepted residence document. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A18
A valid license is among the documents accepted to establish residence. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A18
A Nebraska voter-registration card is one accepted residence document. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A18
A lease or rental agreement used for residence proof must give the landlord’s name and contact information. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A18
A mortgage agreement is among the accepted principal-address documents. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F41 | anchor: A18
A Nebraska DMV renewal notice is among the accepted principal-address documents. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F42 | anchor: A18
A blank check or deposit slip is among the accepted principal-address documents. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F43 | anchor: A18
If Social Security proof is requested, it must show the complete number. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F44 | anchor: A18
The DMV verifies Social Security numbers and documents from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F45 | anchor: A18
A Social Security card is an accepted form of Social Security proof. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F46 | anchor: A18
Form W-2 is among the documents accepted as Social Security number proof. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F47 | anchor: A18
Form SSA-1099 is among the documents accepted as Social Security number proof. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F48 | anchor: A17
Present one document from the handbook’s accepted list to establish U.S. citizenship or lawful status and identity. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F49 | anchor: A17
A city- or county-issued birth certificate may require additional identification documents. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F50 | anchor: A17
A Refugee-stamped I-94 or I-94A may require an I-797. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F51 | anchor: A17
Forms I-151, I-94W and I-94 Border Crosser are not accepted for this identity and lawful-status documentation pathway. [A17]
Source: [A17 -> pdf-0017]

FACT_ID: sec02-F52 | anchor: A18
An unexpired ADIT stamp documenting temporary lawful admission for permanent residence until a stated date is accepted in a valid foreign passport. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

FACT_ID: sec02-F53 | anchor: A18
For the temporary-resident endorsement wording specified after June 28, 2004, the valid foreign passport must show the one-year temporary I-551 permanent-resident statement with the properly placed admission stamp. [A18]
Source: [A18 -> pdf-0018]

Misconceptions: Passing a drive test does not remove identification requirements or license restrictions.
Mnemonics: Documents, vision, written, drive: check each requirement for the applicable path.
Glossary: Principal address means the applicant’s Nebraska residence address; a restriction limits the licensed driving privilege.
Dynamic facts: Changing contacts, officials, live services and fees are withheld from the stable rule inventory.

## C2 — Application documents, testing and license conditions

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A19
A pay stub showing the applicant’s name and Social Security number can serve as Social Security number proof. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A19
A Nebraska document issued to an applicant with parolee immigration status is marked as unsuitable for federal identification. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A19
A parolee applicant still must meet the ordinary identification, verification and testing requirements. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A19
All noncommercial permit and operator-license applicants receive a vision test. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A19
The DMV’s vision screening checks both visual acuity and peripheral vision. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A19
When corrective lenses are necessary to meet the vision standard, the driver must wear them whenever driving. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A19
If the DMV vision standards are not met, an ophthalmologist or optometrist must check the findings. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A19
A person who cannot meet the minimum vision standard cannot receive a license. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A19
Each license class has a separate written test. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A19
The manual supplies written-test material for school learner, learner, school, provisional and Class O operator applicants. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A19
The drive test checks the applicant’s operation of the requested vehicle class in ordinary driving conditions. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A19
Licensing staff may require a drive test from any license applicant at their discretion. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A19
The applicant must provide a drive-test vehicle representative of the requested license class. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A19
The drive-test vehicle must be mechanically sound and have functioning brake lights. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A19
A drive-test vehicle from model year 1964 or later must have a clean working passenger belt for licensing staff. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A19
A drive-test vehicle from model year 1973 or later needs clean working belts for both staff and driver. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R17 | anchor: A19
The drive-test vehicle needs a working speedometer. [A19]
Source: [A19 -> pdf-0019]

FACT_ID: sec02-R18 | anchor: A20
The drive-test vehicle’s interior must be clean. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R19 | anchor: A20
The drive test may assess starting, stopping, turning, lane position, traffic controls, speed, right of way, parking and backing. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R20 | anchor: A20
After three consecutive Class O drive-test failures, reapplication requires proof of successful completion of a DMV-approved driver-training course or at least ninety days holding a learner permit. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R21 | anchor: A20
An applicant denied the requested document receives a Return for Services form explaining the denial. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R22 | anchor: A20
Bring the Return for Services form on the next licensing-office visit. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R23 | anchor: A20
A failed test cannot be repeated that same day. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R24 | anchor: A20
Present the issuance certificate within ninety days to a county treasurer outside Douglas, Lancaster and Sarpy Counties, or to a state driver-licensing office in one of those three counties. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R25 | anchor: A20
Missing the issuance-certificate deadline requires a return to the licensing office. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R26 | anchor: A20
The temporary receipt issued after payment is valid for 30 days. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R27 | anchor: A20
The temporary receipt is not accepted by the TSA as identification for boarding an aircraft or entering certain federal facilities. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R28 | anchor: A20
The permanent document is mailed to the address supplied to licensing staff and is not forwarded by the postal service. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R29 | anchor: A20
Applicants needing disability accommodations should contact the local licensing office or state DMV before testing. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R30 | anchor: A20
An applicant may appeal a licensing or identification-card refusal to the DMV Director. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R31 | anchor: A23
A safety concern reported by police, a physician or another person can lead the DMV to recall a driver for reexamination. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R32 | anchor: A23
A driver recalled for reexamination receives a letter identifying the office, date and time for written and drive tests. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R33 | anchor: A23
A recalled driver must supply a licensed physician’s driving-related medical statement and a vision statement from an optometrist or ophthalmologist. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R34 | anchor: A23
Failure to attend reexamination, provide required statements or pass required tests results in license cancellation. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R35 | anchor: A25
A Nebraska license issued to a U.S. citizen younger than twenty-one expires on the holder’s twenty-first birthday. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R36 | anchor: A25
A Nebraska license issued to a U.S. citizen aged at least twenty-one expires on the holder’s birthday in the fifth year after issuance. [A25]
Source: [A25 -> pdf-0025]

FACT_ID: sec02-R37 | anchor: A24
A changed name or address must be reported through the required document change within 60 days. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R38 | anchor: A24
Issuing a replacement license invalidates the previous document for identification use. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R39 | anchor: A24
Restriction B means corrective lenses are required. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R40 | anchor: A24
Restriction C identifies mechanical aids on the vehicle. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R41 | anchor: A24
Restriction E limits the license to an automatic-transmission vehicle. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R42 | anchor: A24
Restriction F requires outside mirrors. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R43 | anchor: A24
Restriction G limits driving to daylight. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R44 | anchor: A24
Restriction Q prohibits interstate driving. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R45 | anchor: A24
Restriction U requires automatic turn signals. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R46 | anchor: A24
Restriction V limits driving to the stated geographical area. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R47 | anchor: A24
Restriction W excludes one-way roads. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R48 | anchor: A24
Restriction X specifies a maximum driving speed. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R49 | anchor: A24
Restriction Y limits travel to two-lane roads carrying traffic in both directions. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R50 | anchor: A24
Restriction Z represents a special DMV-specified condition. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R51 | anchor: A24
Outside a renewal period, removing a restriction imposed from a medical or vision statement requires the applicable new physician or vision statement. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R52 | anchor: A24
A veteran designation requires eligibility certification through the Nebraska Department of Veterans’ Affairs. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

FACT_ID: sec02-R53 | anchor: A21
Voter registration is offered when applying for a Nebraska license or State ID Card. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R54 | anchor: A22
A permit, license or State ID holder aged sixteen or older may make an organ-and-tissue donation declaration through the DMV. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R55 | anchor: A22
A heart donor symbol appears on the document only when the holder chooses organ or tissue donation. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R56 | anchor: A22
For a donor between sixteen and eighteen, available parents or legal adult guardians may amend the minor’s donation decision. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R57 | anchor: A22
Donor status remains in place when the driving or identification document expires. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R58 | anchor: A23
A donation declared through a permit, license, State ID, donor card or donor registry cannot be rescinded after the donor’s death. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R59 | anchor: A23
A deceased donor’s family is included in the donation process but does not need to authorize the donation. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R60 | anchor: A23
A replacement document is available when the prior card has been lost or destroyed. [A23]
Source: [A23 -> pdf-0023]

FACT_ID: sec02-R61 | anchor: A24
A changed name or a move is a reason to obtain a replacement document. [A24]
Source: [A24 -> pdf-0024]

Authored pedagogic emphasis: An unexpired employment-authorization card is an accepted lawful-status and identity document.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A Certificate of Naturalization on Form N-550 or N-570 is an accepted citizenship and identity document.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: The handbook lists a Certificate of Citizenship on Form N-560 or N-451 as citizenship and identity evidence.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A State Department Consular Report of Birth Abroad on Form FS-240, DS-1350 or FS-545 is accepted as citizenship and identity evidence.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Principal-address evidence must show the Nebraska address and come from 2 different issuing sources.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A post-office box does not establish the principal residence address.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: An applicant younger than 21 who cannot supply personal residence proof may use the parent’s or guardian’s address documents.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A bank or other financial-institution statement used for residence proof must have been issued within 90 days.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A pay stub used for residence proof must be from the preceding 90 days and show the employer’s name and address.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A government document used under the handbook’s recent-document category must have been issued within 90 days.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A magazine used for residence proof must be from the preceding 90 days.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A mailed envelope, box or postcard used as address proof must show a postmark or stamped date within 90 days.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Correspondence, a receipt or an invoice used in the recent-address-document category must be dated within 90 days.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A valid Nebraska vehicle registration is one accepted residence document.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A valid insurance policy or card for life, health, auto or home coverage is one accepted residence document.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A valid real-estate tax statement or receipt is one accepted residence document.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A valid license is among the documents accepted to establish residence.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A Nebraska voter-registration card is one accepted residence document.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A lease or rental agreement used for residence proof must give the landlord’s name and contact information.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A mortgage agreement is among the accepted principal-address documents.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A Nebraska DMV renewal notice is among the accepted principal-address documents.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A blank check or deposit slip is among the accepted principal-address documents.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: If Social Security proof is requested, it must show the complete number.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: The DMV verifies Social Security numbers and documents from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A Social Security card is an accepted form of Social Security proof.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Form W-2 is among the documents accepted as Social Security number proof.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Form SSA-1099 is among the documents accepted as Social Security number proof.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Present one document from the handbook’s accepted list to establish U.S. citizenship or lawful status and identity.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A city- or county-issued birth certificate may require additional identification documents.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A Refugee-stamped I-94 or I-94A may require an I-797.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Forms I-151, I-94W and I-94 Border Crosser are not accepted for this identity and lawful-status documentation pathway.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: An unexpired ADIT stamp documenting temporary lawful admission for permanent residence until a stated date is accepted in a valid foreign passport.

Authored pedagogic emphasis: For the temporary-resident endorsement wording specified after June 28, 2004, the valid foreign passport must show the one-year temporary I-551 permanent-resident statement with the properly placed admission stamp.

high_yield_ranked.domain: Application documents, testing and license conditions

ranked.label: Authored pedagogic emphasis: A pay stub showing the applicant’s name and Social Security number can serve as Social Security number proof.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A Nebraska document issued to an applicant with parolee immigration status is marked as unsuitable for federal identification.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A parolee applicant still must meet the ordinary identification, verification and testing requirements.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: All noncommercial permit and operator-license applicants receive a vision test.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: The DMV’s vision screening checks both visual acuity and peripheral vision.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: When corrective lenses are necessary to meet the vision standard, the driver must wear them whenever driving.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: If the DMV vision standards are not met, an ophthalmologist or optometrist must check the findings.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A person who cannot meet the minimum vision standard cannot receive a license.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Each license class has a separate written test.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: The manual supplies written-test material for school learner, learner, school, provisional and Class O operator applicants.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: The drive test checks the applicant’s operation of the requested vehicle class in ordinary driving conditions.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Licensing staff may require a drive test from any license applicant at their discretion.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: The applicant must provide a drive-test vehicle representative of the requested license class.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: The drive-test vehicle must be mechanically sound and have functioning brake lights.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A drive-test vehicle from model year 1964 or later must have a clean working passenger belt for licensing staff.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A drive-test vehicle from model year 1973 or later needs clean working belts for both staff and driver.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: The drive-test vehicle needs a working speedometer.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: The drive-test vehicle’s interior must be clean.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: The drive test may assess starting, stopping, turning, lane position, traffic controls, speed, right of way, parking and backing.

Authored pedagogic emphasis: After three consecutive Class O drive-test failures, reapplication requires proof of successful completion of a DMV-approved driver-training course or at least ninety days holding a learner permit.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: An applicant denied the requested document receives a Return for Services form explaining the denial.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Bring the Return for Services form on the next licensing-office visit.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A failed test cannot be repeated that same day.

Authored pedagogic emphasis: Present the issuance certificate within ninety days to a county treasurer outside Douglas, Lancaster and Sarpy Counties, or to a state driver-licensing office in one of those three counties.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Missing the issuance-certificate deadline requires a return to the licensing office.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: The temporary receipt issued after payment is valid for 30 days.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: The temporary receipt is not accepted by the TSA as identification for boarding an aircraft or entering certain federal facilities.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: The permanent document is mailed to the address supplied to licensing staff and is not forwarded by the postal service.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Applicants needing disability accommodations should contact the local licensing office or state DMV before testing.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: An applicant may appeal a licensing or identification-card refusal to the DMV Director.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A safety concern reported by police, a physician or another person can lead the DMV to recall a driver for reexamination.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A driver recalled for reexamination receives a letter identifying the office, date and time for written and drive tests.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A recalled driver must supply a licensed physician’s driving-related medical statement and a vision statement from an optometrist or ophthalmologist.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Failure to attend reexamination, provide required statements or pass required tests results in license cancellation.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A Nebraska license issued to a U.S. citizen younger than twenty-one expires on the holder’s twenty-first birthday.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A Nebraska license issued to a U.S. citizen aged at least twenty-one expires on the holder’s birthday in the fifth year after issuance.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A changed name or address must be reported through the required document change within 60 days.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Issuing a replacement license invalidates the previous document for identification use.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Restriction B means corrective lenses are required.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Restriction C identifies mechanical aids on the vehicle.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Restriction E limits the license to an automatic-transmission vehicle.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Restriction F requires outside mirrors.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Restriction G limits driving to daylight.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Restriction Q prohibits interstate driving.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Restriction U requires automatic turn signals.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Restriction V limits driving to the stated geographical area.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Restriction W excludes one-way roads.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Restriction X specifies a maximum driving speed.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Restriction Y limits travel to two-lane roads carrying traffic in both directions.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Restriction Z represents a special DMV-specified condition.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Outside a renewal period, removing a restriction imposed from a medical or vision statement requires the applicable new physician or vision statement.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A veteran designation requires eligibility certification through the Nebraska Department of Veterans’ Affairs.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Voter registration is offered when applying for a Nebraska license or State ID Card.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A permit, license or State ID holder aged sixteen or older may make an organ-and-tissue donation declaration through the DMV.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A heart donor symbol appears on the document only when the holder chooses organ or tissue donation.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: For a donor between sixteen and eighteen, available parents or legal adult guardians may amend the minor’s donation decision.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: Donor status remains in place when the driving or identification document expires.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A donation declared through a permit, license, State ID, donor card or donor registry cannot be rescinded after the donor’s death.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A deceased donor’s family is included in the donation process but does not need to authorize the donation.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A replacement document is available when the prior card has been lost or destroyed.
Authored pedagogic emphasis: A changed name or a move is a reason to obtain a replacement document.
